recipes.name: Endive mash and Dutch meatballs
ingredients: Potatoes, endive cabbage, milk, mustard, butter, ground black pepper, kosher salt, ground nutmeg, vinegar, bacon (or pork belly).
Ground beef and pork, mustard, ketjap manis, kosher salt, ground black pepper, ground nutmeg, eggs, bread crumbs, butter
instructions: Cut 250 grams (about ½ pound) of bacon into small pieces and cook until crispy. Set aside.
Cut a whole bunch of endive (400-500 grams: 1 pound) into thin strips. Wash, drain, and set aside.
Boil water in a large pot for the potatoes.
Peel 1 kg (2.2 pounds) of potatoes. Clean them, cut into large chunks, and put them into boiling water until cooked.
Drain and mash the potatoes. Add ½ cup of milk little by little to make a smooth puree.
Add the bacon, 1 tbs mustard, 2 tbs butter, 1 ts ground nutmeg, 1 ts ground black pepper, and ¼ ts kosher salt, and mix it well.
Add the shredded endive bit by bit to allow it to shrink a little as you go.
Add 1-2 ts vinegar and mix it well.

Mix these ingredients in a bowl by hand until well combined and sticky: 500 grams of ground beef and pork mix, 2 tbs mustard, 2 tbs ketjap manis, ¼ ts kosher salt, ½ ts ground black pepper, 1 ts ground nutmeg, ⅓ cup bread crumbs, and 2 eggs. *tip: You can replace 2 tbs ketjap manis with 2 tbs soy sauce and ½ tbs brown sugar
Divide the mixture into 4 large balls.
Heat up a covered pot or pan with over medium high heat.
Add ¼ cup butter and wait until it turns brown.
Cook the meatballs until all sides are golden brown.
Turn down the heat and simmer for about 25-30 minutes. Flip occasionally until thoroughly cooked.
Take the meatballs out of the pot out and set aside.
Add ¼ cup water to the pot and cook over low heat to make gravy. You can add 1 ts flour to make it sticky.
